subject: Implementation kickoff: model shortlist + traffic & context planning
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Implementation kickoff: model shortlist + traffic & context planning

Jordan — good to connect. As discussed during sales handoff, this thread will be the working channel for the implementation work: model selection, context-length needs, and token-volume estimates so we can produce a recommended capacity and rollout plan.

Quick agenda for the upcoming tech workshop (see attachment: redwood_impl_kickoff_agenda.md):
- Confirm inference surface (chat API, document Q&A, embeddings, reranking)
- Finalize model shortlist candidates and max context requirements
- Review token volume & concurrency estimates for first 90 days
- Decide on caching/batching strategy and initial quantization profile

What I need from you before the workshop: rough numbers for expected daily active users (DAU), average session length in turns, and any peak-period multipliers (e.g., marketing sends, EOD batch jobs). You mentioned 2 distinct use cases in our discovery — please call them out in the reply so we map traffic per flow.

Prelim info from our side (attached: token_traffic_estimates.xlsx):
- We’ll shortlist a latency-optimized medium model and a higher-capacity context model (details to follow).
- For 8k context workflows, target baseline: ~12–18 tokens/sec inference throughput per request (token growth depends on prompt+response length).

I’m copying Monica (CS lead) and Priyom (solutions engineer) to drop an initial model shortlist and sizing assumptions. Can we lock a 60-minute tech workshop next Tue or Wed?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.inference
+1 415-555-0192

Attachment stubs: redwood_impl_kickoff_agenda.md (3 items), token_traffic_estimates.xlsx (sheet: traffic_by_flow), model_shortlist_v1.pdf (summary)

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@finlytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
Cc: onboarding@finlytics.com
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff: model shortlist + traffic & context planning

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the clear agenda. Quick answers to your pre-work items to help the sizing exercise:

Use cases (two flows):
1) "Client Assist" (chat-support + knowledge base lookup): expected 3,500 DAU at launch, average session 6 turns, typical prompt + response ~600 tokens total, peaks 3x during product releases.
2) "Batch Summarization" (daily overnight job): ~2,000 docs/day, average doc length ~3,500 tokens, expected bulk requests concentrated between 02:00–06:00 UTC (peak concurrency ~40).

Non-functional constraints:
- Latency target for Client Assist: 400–700ms tail for 95th pct to preserve chat feel.
- Data residency: all inference must run in us-west region for now.

We don’t have a strict budget cap yet, but price-sensitivity will matter if monthly token spend > $50k.

We can meet Wed 12 May 2027 at 16:00 UTC for the workshop. Please send an invite with dial-in.

—Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Product| FinLytics
jordan.price@finlytics.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff: model shortlist + traffic & context planning

Jordan / team — I pulled together a pragmatic shortlist and a first-pass sizing table (attached: model_shortlist_v1.pdf and token_traffic_estimates.xlsx sheet: assumptions). Summary below — this is intentionally conservative so we can iterate during the workshop.

Model shortlist (initial candidates):
- Option A (latency-optimized): Mistral-Chat-8B / quantized int8 — good  latency, fits Client Assist 400–700ms with batching and prefix caching for KB lookups. Context cap: 8k.
- Option B (balanced throughput + quality): LlamaX-13B-16k variant — better at multi-turn and longer prompts; target 16k context for mixed chat + doc snippets.
- Option C (high-context, long-form): RedAlpha-32k (server variant) — for Batch Summarization and long-doc Q&A; expect higher cost but reduces truncation/segmentation work.

Sizing assumptions (first 90 days):
- Client Assist: 3,500 DAU, avg 6 turns, avg tokens per turn (prompt+resp) ~100 -> per-day tokens ≈ 3,500*6*100 = 2.1M tokens. Peak concurrency (3x) considered for capacity planning.
- Batch Summarization: 2,000 docs/day * 3,500 tokens ≈ 7.0M tokens/day. Bulk window 02:00–06:00 UTC, peak concurrency ~40.
- Combined baseline daily tokens ≈ 9.1M tokens/day; monthly ≈ 273M tokens (30d).

Estimated cost/throughput notes (very rough):
- If Client Assist runs on Option A (Mistral-Chat-8B int8), expect per-token compute lower, with ability to scale horizontally on small GPU instances.
- For batch summarization, Option C (RedAlpha-32k) reduces pre-processing overhead of splitting long docs; we can also explore streaming summarization to lower peak memory.

Operational recommendations:
1) Start with hybrid deployment: Option A for interactive chat traffic (to meet latency) + Option C reserved capacity for nightly batches.
2) Enable prefix caching for KB lookups (saves ~40% token work for repeat queries).
3) Use dynamic batching with a 20–50ms max-queue target to preserve chat tail latency.
4) Quantize interactive model to int8 while validating quality against your prompt suite; keep a float16 variant available for A/B verification.
5) Canary rollout: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% across 2 weeks, monitor latency, prompt-quality regressions, and cost metrics.

I added a short sample capacity calc in token_traffic_estimates.xlsx (sheet: capacity_calc) with GPU sizing guidance (per-GPU QPS/token throughput rows). We should walk these numbers in the workshop and finalize commit levels if you want reserved capacity for Batch Summarization windows.

Proposed next steps:
- Lock workshop (Jordan proposed 12 May 2027 16:00 UTC) — I’ll send calendar + pre-read.
- Jordan: confirm whether batch summarization must run on dedicated reserved capacity or can run on preemptible / burstable pools.
- Kimberly/Monica: confirm security controls (S3 ingestion, E2E logs) for the batch flow.

Happy to expand any of the calc rows ahead of the workshop.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.inference

Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff: model shortlist + traffic & context planning

Jordan — thanks for the details and for confirming the Wed workshop date. Calendar invite sent for 2027-05-12 16:00 UTC with dial-in and pre-read links (Drive + HubSpot).

A couple of logistics items ahead of the session:
- Please upload a small representative sample (2–3 anonymized transcripts for Client Assist and 3 sample docs for Batch Summarization) to the shared Drive folder so Priyom can run quick quality checks on the shortlist. Link in invite.
- For the nightly batch, if you can confirm whether the pipeline can tolerate queued retries (yes/no), it changes how aggressively we size reserved capacity.
- Monica will start a short risk register for security/compliance items; Jordan, if there are additional vendor questionnaires (e.g., SOC/Security checklist), please attach to the Drive folder.

We’ll use the workshop to lock the final shortlist and produce a recommended initial capacity + a two-week canary plan. If the numbers in Priyom’s worksheet look reasonable we’ll also draft an optional dedicated pool quote for the batch window.

See you Wed 12 May.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.inference
